Markets.title: Dalal Street Week Ahead: Can Nifty defend the 23,000 support zone?
Markets.summary: Nifty enters the week in a corrective, range-bound setup with crucial support at the 23,000–23,100 zone and resistance at 23,500. While a sustained move above 23,500 could trigger a rebound, dropping below 23,000 may deepen the market correction.

Markets.title: Bank of India MF CIO Alok Singh sees banks poised for a re-rating. Here’s what could trigger it
Markets.summary: Bank of India Mutual Fund CIO Alok Singh believes strong loan growth, healthy returns, and low non-performing assets will drive a re-rating for banks. He also expects upcoming policy announcements and robust business figures to alleviate concerns regarding profit margins and foreign currency flows.

Markets.title: Bitcoin reclaims $80,000, Ethereum nears $2,620 despite hawkish Fed, CLARITY Act setback
Markets.summary: Bitcoin surpassed $80,000 and Ethereum neared $2,620 as cryptocurrency markets rebounded. The recovery occurred despite a hawkish Federal Reserve, regulatory uncertainty surrounding the CLARITY Act, and ongoing ETF outflows.

Markets.title: Warren Buffett sounds alarm as stock market warning returns for only second time in 155 years
Markets.summary: Warren Buffett is warning of extreme stock valuations as the S&P 500's CAPE ratio reaches rare historical levels. While this indicator signals weaker long-term returns, Buffett's strategy focuses on durable cash flows and businesses that compound across market cycles.

Data & Insights.summary: Veteran banker Uday Kotak outlined a seven-point strategy for India to achieve its 'Viksit Bharat 2047' goal amid global uncertainty. His recommendations emphasize stronger fiscal discipline, capital-attracting reforms, and enhanced manufacturing capabilities.

Data & Insights.summary: Economic Affairs Secretary Anuradha Thakur stated that private sector investment is essential for India's Viksit Bharat vision because government budgets cannot meet financing needs alone. Additionally, NK Singh called for higher savings and greater mobilization of private capital to support this goal.

Data & Insights.title: States need to raise capex to 3% of GSDP by FY32 for developed India: Revenue secretary
Data & Insights.summary: Revenue Secretary Arvind Shrivastava stated that Indian states must increase their capital expenditure to 3% of their GSDP by FY32. Achieving this target is necessary to support India's goal of becoming a developed economy by 2047.

Data & Insights.title: India needs more savings, private capital to sustain 7-8% growth, says N.K. Singh
Data & Insights.summary: Former finance commission chairman N.K. Singh stated that India must increase domestic savings and private capital to maintain a 7% to 8% economic growth rate. He added that achieving this requires improved capital allocation and stronger fiscal coordination between the central and state governments.
